symptom: An Ethereum-to-Mezo Native Bridge tracker marks an ERC-20 transfer completed when the logless Mezo system bridge transaction succeeds or the accepted sequence advances, without proving the recipient received the mapped token.
prerequisites: The tracker observes a successful Mezo system transaction carrying bridge((uint256,address,uint256,address)[]) or a matching sequence tip.
The transferred source token should mint a mapped ERC-20 representation on Mezo.
diagnosticSteps: Assert both networks, pin the Ethereum AssetsLocked receipt and matching Mezo system transaction, and compare the full sequence, recipient, source token, and raw amount tuple.
Read the deployed source-token mapping at the destination block and verify the expected mapped token and decimals.
Compare recipient mapped-token state immediately before and at the destination block, or obtain equivalent delivery proof; do not use the empty system receipt logs as mint evidence.
expected: A successful destination system transaction or advanced sequence proves recipient ERC-20 delivery.
observed: The deployed v12 keeper can skip a blocked recipient, missing mapping, or failed external ERC-20 mint while continuing the accepted sequence. The representative completed USDC trace required an exact 5,000,000,000-raw-unit recipient balance delta in addition to the system payload and sequence change.
control: For the recorded sequence 34490, the source event, destination payload, deployed mapping, sequence transition, token decimals, and recipient balance delta all agree exactly.
verifiedCause: Native Bridge inbound sequence acceptance and recipient ERC-20 delivery are distinct facts in the version-matched deployed keeper. The system bridge call is an observability projection of consensus processing, not a user-callable mint receipt with ERC-20 logs.
safeMitigation: Model the successful system transaction as destination progress. For ERC-20 terminal success, require the mapped representation and recipient post-state or equivalent delivery proof. Keep missing delivery pending or ambiguous and escalate for recovery; never replay or resubmit value from receipt absence alone.
limitations: This diagnosis is scoped to the recorded active v12 source and must be rechecked after client/keeper upgrades.
The positive representative trace proves the stronger completion method; it does not assert that a skipped mint occurred in that transaction.
This record does not authorize a Native Bridge writer or define a recovery transaction.
